learning_outcomes.text: Know the existing regulations on energy saving in industry.
Know the primary energy demand in industry.
Determine energy recovery in industrial processes and the operation of systems.
Know the existing regulations on energy efficiency in buildings (residential and domestic sectors and tertiary or service sectors).
Establish building improvements related to efficiency (envelope and installations).
Determine the energy demand of buildings (in residential and tertiary).
Calculate and analyze the energy rating of buildings.
Know the methodology for conducting energy audits in buildings and their associated installations.
Learn to use equipment and instruments associated with the energy evaluation of buildings.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and definitions of energy saving. Saving in industrial facilities. Utilization and saving of energy in thermal and electrical energy production facilities. Operation of energy systems in industry and their saving possibilities.
Thermal energy recovery in different processes. Types of industrial thermal processes. Heat recuperators in industry. Types of heat recuperators. Calculation and selection of heat recuperators.

Energy situation in buildings. Regulations. Basic concepts and Regulations in Building. Basic Document DB HE "Energy Saving" of the Technical Building Code. Calculation of characteristic envelope parameters. Limitation of energy demand. Practical applications.

Installations and energy systems in buildings and their effect on building energy consumption. Regulations on energy rating and certification of buildings. Limitation of energy consumption and energy rating. Practical applications.
Concept of energy audit in buildings. Equipment for energy evaluation of buildings.
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices (identification and analysis of heat recuperators, use of measurement equipment for thermal analysis, thermography)
Practical work (application of energy efficiency measures in a building, development of a practical work on energy saving in buildings)

assessment_methods.method: Resolution and delivery of proposed assignments, projects, and practical work

assessment_rules: There are two evaluation paths: continuous evaluation and global evaluation. For continuous evaluation, the final grade is 60% from the written final exam (requiring a minimum of 3 out of 10 points to be applied), 30% from proposed assignments and practical work (10% for industry topics, 20% for building topics), and 10% from attendance and class participation. The final exam and proposed assignments are recoverable in the extraordinary call; attendance and participation are not. For global evaluation, chosen by the student, a single exam is conducted on the final exam day, consisting of Part I (80% of final grade, theoretical/practical questions) and Part II (20% of final grade, additional written test on competencies related to exercises and assignments).
